name: Combining multiple models and methods together
gist: These papers explore how to merge different models, combine multiple reasoning paths, and use multiple models working together to solve harder problems.
explain: A single model, no matter how large, has limitations—it might be good at math but weak at writing, or fast but not very accurate. Papers in this area explore merging different models so they complement each other, and combining different reasoning paths so the model can try multiple approaches and pick the best one. One technique is ensemble methods, where multiple models solve the same problem and their answers are combined by voting or averaging. Another is routing, where different problems get sent to different models optimized for those specific tasks. A third is model merging, where researchers take parameters from multiple models and combine them into a single model that tries to keep the best abilities of each.

The challenge is that combining models usually requires more computation—running five models to get one answer takes five times as much processing, which costs money and time. So papers study which combinations are worth the cost by measuring the accuracy gain against the computation cost, how to prune away redundancy to reduce wasted parallel processing, and how to route efficiently so you only run the models you need. Some papers explore mixture-of-experts architectures where a model decides which internal components to use for each input, which can be more efficient than running separate models because most examples do not need all components. The question becomes: what is the right tradeoff between accuracy and cost?

The result is systems that are more accurate and harder to break than single models because failures are caught by redundancy. In safety-critical applications, combining multiple approaches reduces the chance that a single model's failure will cause a problem because you have backups. This also mirrors how humans solve hard problems—we think about it from multiple angles and synthesize insights, not snap to an answer instantly, which is why human teams survive mistakes that would kill individuals. Papers show that thoughtful combination works better than just stacking the best parts together because diversity of approaches catches errors no single model would catch since different models make different mistakes.

papers.title: A Problem-Oriented Perspective and Anchor Verification for Code Optimization
papers.contribution: Significantly enhances both correct optimization ratio and speedup through global algorithmic innovation enabled by problem-centric approach.

papers.title: Agentic Collaboration as an Information Bottleneck Problem
papers.contribution: Mutual information strongly predicts downstream performance independent of task, and larger compressors are 1.6× more accurate and 4.6× more token-efficient.

papers.title: An Ensemble Framework for Unbiased Language Model Watermarking
papers.contribution: Substantially reduces tokens needed for reliable detection and increases resistance to smoothing and paraphrasing attacks without compromising generation quality.

papers.title: Certain Head, Uncertain Tail: Expert-Sample for Test-Time Scaling in Fine-Grained MoE
papers.contribution: Expert-Sample consistently improves pass@n and verification-based accuracy; on Qwen3-30B pass@32 rises from 85.4% to 91.9% with Best-of-N verification reaching 62.6%.

papers.title: Language Model Networks: Supervision-Efficient Learning through Dense Communication
papers.contribution: Achieves task performance improvement with small additional training cost and effective adaptation under limited supervision.

papers.title: MAS-ProVe: Understanding the Process Verification of Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that process-level verification does not consistently improve performance and frequently exhibits high variance; LLM-as-a-Judge outperforms reward-based approaches.

papers.title: MASPO: Joint Prompt Optimization for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: MASPO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art prompt optimization methods with an average accuracy improvement of 2.9 across six diverse tasks.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Design: Optimizing Agents with Better Prompts and Topologies
papers.contribution: MASS-optimized systems substantially outperform existing alternatives and reveal design principles for building effective multi-agent systems.

papers.title: Best-of-Infinity: Asymptotic Performance of Test-Time Compute
papers.contribution: Efficiently allocates inference-time computation while improving performance through weighted mixture of multiple LLMs.

papers.title: Can LLM Agents Stick to the Script? Modeling Commitment in Interactive Narratives
papers.contribution: Reveals that linguistic quality does not guarantee commitment preservation; best model (GPT-5.2) achieves only 40% survival rate after 20 turns with 40-68% fact conflict rates.

papers.title: Decouple Searching from Training: Scaling Data Mixing via Model Merging for Large Language Model Pre-training
papers.contribution: Breaks the trade-off between sufficiency, accuracy, and efficiency; obtains optimal mixture with higher benchmark performance at lower search cost; releases 22T-token DeMix Corpora.

papers.title: DiSRouter: Distributed Self-Routing for LLM Selections
papers.contribution: DiSRouter outperforms existing routing methods in utility across scenarios, effectively distinguishes easy from hard queries, and generalizes to out-of-domain tasks.

papers.title: DoVer: Intervention-Driven Auto Debugging for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: DoVer flips 18-28% of failed trials into successes, achieves up to 16% milestone progress, and validates or refutes 30-60% of failure hypotheses.

papers.title: EntropyLong: Effective Long-Context Training via Predictive Uncertainty
papers.contribution: Models trained on EntropyLong-constructed 128K sequences show significant improvements on RULER benchmarks and LongBench-v2 for long-context understanding.

papers.title: EvoGM: Learning to Merge LLMs via Evolutionary Generative Optimization
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines exhibiting robust performance on both seen and unseen tasks.

papers.title: FUSE: Ensembling Verifiers with Zero Labeled Data
papers.contribution: Matches or improves semi-supervised alternatives without any labeled data across diverse generators, verifiers, and benchmarks including GPQA Diamond and IMO questions.

papers.title: IPMark: A Sentence-Level Watermark for LLMs with Hierarchical Personalization and Efficient Detection
papers.contribution: Achieves the lowest perplexity among baselines while maintaining strong robustness, significantly reducing detection latency through hierarchical retrieval.

papers.title: Model Merging Scaling Laws in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Enables predictive planning to estimate experts needed for target loss and trade off base model scaling versus adding experts, with gains roughly as 1/k.

papers.title: OptMerge: Unifying Multimodal LLM Capabilities and Modalities via Model Merging
papers.contribution: The proposed method achieves an average performance gain of 2.48% and demonstrates that model merging enables building improved MLLMs without training data.

papers.title: Orthogonal Model Merging
papers.contribution: Mitigates catastrophic forgetting and maintains model performance across diverse tasks via principled geometry-aware integration.

papers.title: Post-Hoc Merging is Not Enough: Many-Shot Model Merging with Loss-Gap Balancing
papers.contribution: Improves multi-task performance with significant gains on worst-performing tasks, effectively mitigating information erasure across task-specific models.

papers.title: Propose, Solve, Verify: Self-Play Through Formal Verification
papers.contribution: Improves pass@1 by up to 9.6x over inference-only and expert-iteration baselines on three benchmarks.

papers.title: ProtocolBench: Which LLM MultiAgent Protocol to Choose?
papers.contribution: Demonstrates 36.5% variation in completion time across protocols; ProtocolRouter reduces Fail-Storm recovery by 18.1% versus best single-protocol baseline.

papers.title: Rethinking LLM Ensembling from the Perspective of Mixture Models
papers.contribution: Achieves 1.78x-2.68x faster inference than conventional ensembling while maintaining equivalent performance, mathematically equivalent to sampling from ensemble distribution.

papers.title: SWE-IF: Aligning Code Evaluation with Human Preference
papers.contribution: Composite score of both metrics correlates best with human preference, with instruction following as primary differentiator among 31 LLMs tested.

papers.title: Sampling from Your Language Model One Byte at a Time
papers.contribution: Solves PBP and enables LLM ensemble/post-training transfer with different tokenizers.

papers.title: Trinity: An Evolved LLM Coordinator
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance including 86.2% on LiveCodeBench, consistently outperforming individual models.

papers.title: V1: Unifying Generation and Self-Verification for Parallel Reasoners
papers.contribution: Improves Pass@1 by up to 10% on code generation and benchmarks while outperforming best-of-n and providing more efficient test-time scaling.

papers.title: Verification and Co-Alignment via Heterogeneous Consistency for Preference-Aligned LLM Annotations
papers.contribution: Consistently improves annotation quality across eight NLU datasets, enabling Llama-3-8B to surpass GPT-3.5/4o after co-alignment.
